prompt:
PRIORITY RULES:
1) No text or symbols anywhere: no letters, numbers, signage, logos or inscriptions, no writing on scrolls, tablets, books, boards or halos, and no artist's signature or initials in a corner.
2) One scene painted to every edge of the frame: no panels, collage, border, frame, margin, visible paper or blank backdrop, and never a photographed painting or mockup.
3) Nothing from outside the moment's era.
4) Natural anatomy: no extra or malformed limbs, hands or faces.
5) sexually explicit content and lingering gore are never shown; serious depictions of battles, blood, death and crucifixion and non-sexual nudity may be, treated seriously.
6) No likeness of any real actor, performer or public figure.
7) Show the SELECTED CHARACTERS with their canon. Anyone else appears only as an unnamed figure the scene plan describes.
8) A subject without form is never drawn. Only when it is selected may the light, cloud, smoke, fire or wind in the scene plan stand for it, with nobody in them. A throne or seat stays empty unless the scene plan names who sits on it.
If instructions conflict, follow these rules, then the work brief, then canon, then the art style, then the scene plan. The text decides who is in the scene; canon decides how they look; the scene plan decides this moment's place, time, light, clothing and action. Owner look constraints, when given, are binding.

SCENE: one moment of The Holy Bible, described by the scene plan below.

WORK BRIEF (bible-web; what may be shown; it outranks the style, the look and the plan):
Tone: Reverent, grounded and epic; grief, hope and human dignity without spectacle.
Depiction: the presence has no human face or body; use light, cloud, fire or radiance. The Holy Spirit is dove, wind or flame, never human.
Depiction: Treat battles, death and crucifixion seriously; avoid lingering gore.
Depiction: No sexually explicit content; non-sexual nudity may follow the text.
Depiction: Show all peoples with dignity, without ethnic or religious caricature.
Depiction: Visionary creatures follow the text, strange and fearsome rather than comic.
Era: Creation and the patriarchs
People: Ancient Near Eastern households, herders and farmers.
Dress: Simple wool or linen wraps, tunics and sandals.
Buildings and objects: Wild land, tents, wells, altars and mud-brick towns as the text allows.
Technology: Hand tools, herding, farming and weighed metal; no modern objects.

SELECTED CHARACTERS: (none with fixed canon; show only figures the scene plan describes, or none)

UNSEEN PRESENCE (binding): the light, cloud, smoke, fire and wind in the scene plan are light and weather spread through the place, not one glowing shape. Nobody stands, sits or hovers in them.

SCENE PLAN (this moment's place, time and action; obey the rules, brief, canon and style):
Primary subject: A spreading radiance of pure light, bursting from beyond the frame across the dark waters
Action: Light pushes outward and begins to pierce the primordial darkness over the deep
Setting: Formless wild expanse of dark deep waters beneath an open void, with no land features yet
Secondary elements: Dark waters rippling faintly under the first light, mist and shadow receding at the edges
Mood: Awe, stillness and quiet wonder at the first moment of creation
Time of day: Primordial darkness giving way to the first light, still and unbroken air
Composition: Wide horizontal view over the waters, light entering from above and beyond the frame, darkness fading toward the edges

ART STYLE: Storybook
Rendering: A modern children's picture-book illustration of the work's world: simplified, softly rounded figures with kind, readable faces, flat shapes with light texture, and clear, uncluttered settings.

Lighting: Soft, even daylight or a warm glow; simple shadows and no harsh contrast.
Materials and texture: Flat opaque color with light paper grain and pencil texture inside the shapes.
Composition: Simple, readable staging with one clear focus; generous shapes and background that fill the picture to every edge and corner.

- Depict the moment directly, as if the viewer is present inside the scene.
- Extend scenery, sky, darkness, architecture or atmosphere all the way to the edges and corners.

SCENE: one moment of The Holy Bible, Genesis 22:10: "Abraham stretched out his hand, and took the knife to kill his son."

WORK BRIEF (bible-web; what may be shown; it outranks the style, the look and the plan):
Tone: Reverent, grounded and epic; grief, hope and human dignity without spectacle.
Depiction: God the Father has no human face or body; use light, cloud, fire or radiance. The Holy Spirit is dove, wind or flame, never human.
Depiction: Treat battles, death and crucifixion seriously; avoid lingering gore.
Depiction: No sexually explicit content; non-sexual nudity may follow the text.
Depiction: Show all peoples with dignity, without ethnic or religious caricature.
Depiction: Visionary creatures follow the text, strange and fearsome rather than comic.
Era: Creation and the patriarchs
People: Ancient Near Eastern households, herders and farmers.
Dress: Simple wool or linen wraps, tunics and sandals.
Buildings and objects: Wild land, tents, wells, altars and mud-brick towns as the text allows.
Technology: Hand tools, herding, farming and weighed metal; no modern objects.

SELECTED CHARACTERS: Abram; Isaac, son of Abraham and Sarah

CANON (fixed identity of the figures, places and things present; the scene plan decides pose, expression and action):
- Abram, later Abraham: an elderly man of seventy-five to one hundred years and beyond; lean, weathered build from years of travel; dark skin tanned by desert sun; short greying beard and hair; deep-set, steady eyes and lined face. Signature outfit: a plain undyed wool wrap over a earth-brown linen tunic, leather sandals. Signature prop: a long wooden herder's staff.
- Isaac: a young man in late youth to middle age; lean, sturdy build from herding and labour in the open country; olive-brown skin; dark brown hair cut close at the neck, short beard kept trim; calm, steady face with heavy-lidded, grey-brown eyes that grow dim with age; wears a plain undyed linen tunic with a woollen wrap of earth-brown ochre, and leather sandals; carries a wooden staff of plain olive wood, and a bundle of kindling when bound to the wood at Moriah.
- Mount Moriah: a rocky ridge of pale limestone rising above a dry upland plain, with terraced slopes of scrub, wild thyme, and scattered terebinth trees. On the summit a bare stone outcrop serves as an altar place, with a low ring of unhewn stones. Distant hills fold away in dusty blue haze.
- Only Abram, Isaac, son of Abraham and Sarah, Moriah have this canon look; other selected people get clearly different faces, hair and clothing colours.

SCENE PLAN (this moment's place, time and action; obey the rules, brief, canon and style):
Primary subject: Abraham, an older man in a plain undyed wool wrap, arm raised with a bronze knife, body tense and turned toward the altar.
Action: Abraham's arm is lifted at its highest point, the blade catching the first light, as he is about to strike.
Setting: A bare rocky ridge of Moriah, dry scrub, a rough stone altar stacked with split wood.
Secondary elements: Isaac, bound with cord, lies still on the wood of the altar in a linen tunic; a bundle of firewood and a leather water skin rest on the ground; a few tents and a well visible far below in the valley.
Mood: Solemn, heavy with grief and resolve, quiet and tense.
Time of day: Early morning at first light, pale gold sun rising over the eastern hills, thin dawn haze, still air with a dry wind over the ridge.
Composition: Medium-wide view from the side of the altar, Abraham on the left with raised arm, Isaac on the altar in the centre-right, the valley and rising sun open behind them.

ART STYLE: Storybook
Rendering: A modern children's picture-book illustration of the work's world: simplified, softly rounded figures with kind, readable faces, flat shapes with light texture, and clear, uncluttered settings.
Negatives: The illustration fills the whole image: no white border, page edge, vignette or frame, and no title, caption, speech bubble, lettering or signature. Avoid photorealism, anime, 3D rendering and grotesque caricature; faces stay gentle and proportions stay human.
Palette: Warm, soft but saturated colors: honey yellow, terracotta, sage green, dusty blue and cream, with deep indigo for night scenes.
Lighting: Soft, even daylight or a warm glow; simple shadows and no harsh contrast.
Materials and texture: Flat opaque color with light paper grain and pencil texture inside the shapes.
Composition: Simple, readable staging with one clear focus; generous shapes and background that fill the picture to every edge and corner.

REFERENCE IMAGES (attached after this text, in this order; identity and rendering only, never the composition):
- Image 1: Abram's reference sheet (one figure shown in three views). Match its identity exactly for Abram only; do not copy its poses, layout or plain grey background, and give other selected figures a different face and clothing.
- Image 2: Isaac, son of Abraham and Sarah's reference sheet (one figure shown in three views). Match its identity exactly for Isaac, son of Abraham and Sarah only; do not copy its poses, layout or plain grey background, and give other selected figures a different face and clothing.
Render everything in the ART STYLE above, even where a reference is painted in another style.

NARRATIVE CONTINUITY (cues only; compose the current moment):
- Before: They came to the place which God had told him of. Abraham built the altar there, and laid the wood in order, bound Isaac his son, and laid him on the altar, on the wood.
- After: Yahweh’s angel called to him out of the sky, and said, “Abraham, Abraham!” He said, “Here I am.”

SCENE PRESENTATION:
- Depict the moment directly, as if the viewer is present inside the scene.
- Extend scenery, sky, darkness, architecture or atmosphere all the way to the edges and corners.
Aspect ratio: 16:9 (WIDESCREEN landscape).

PRIORITY RULES:
1) No text or symbols anywhere: no letters, numbers, signage, logos or inscriptions, no writing on scrolls, tablets, books, boards or halos, and no artist's signature or initials in a corner.
2) One scene painted to every edge of the frame: no panels, collage, border, frame, margin, visible paper or blank backdrop, and never a photographed painting or mockup.
3) Nothing from outside the moment's era.

5) sexually explicit content and lingering gore are never shown; serious depictions of battles, blood, death and crucifixion and non-sexual nudity may be, treated seriously.

8) A subject without form is never drawn. Only when it is selected may the light, cloud, smoke, fire or wind in the scene plan stand for it, with nobody in them. A throne or seat stays empty unless the scene plan names who sits on it.
If instructions conflict, follow these rules, then the work brief, then canon, then the art style, then the scene plan. SCENE: one moment of The Holy Bible, described by the scene plan below.

WORK BRIEF (bible-web; what may be shown; it outranks the style, the look and the plan):
Tone: Reverent, grounded and epic; grief, hope and human dignity without spectacle.
Depiction: the presence has no human face or body; use light, cloud, fire or radiance. The Holy Spirit is dove, wind or flame, never human.
Depiction: Treat battles, death and crucifixion seriously; avoid lingering gore.
Depiction: No sexually explicit content; non-sexual nudity may follow the text.
Depiction: Show all peoples with dignity, without ethnic or religious caricature.
Depiction: Visionary creatures follow the text, strange and fearsome rather than comic.
Era: Egypt, wilderness and settlement
People: Israelites, Egyptians and neighboring ancient peoples.
Dress: Woven tunics, cloaks, Egyptian linen and priestly garments.
Buildings and objects: Tents, tabernacle, Egyptian palaces and fortified towns.
Technology: Bronze tools, chariots and early iron; no modern objects.

SELECTED CHARACTERS: Moses; Aaron, brother of Moses

UNSEEN PRESENCE (binding): the light, cloud, smoke, fire and wind in the scene plan are light and weather spread through the place, not one glowing shape. Nobody stands, sits or hovers in them.

CANON (fixed identity of the figures, places and things present; the scene plan decides pose, expression and action):
- Moses: an old man of about eighty; lean, weathered build; brown skin darkened by desert sun; white hair and a long white beard; deep-set, steady eyes and lined brow; a plain undyed linen tunic belted at the waist with a long dark-brown wool cloak; he carries a wooden shepherd's staff of dark acacia wood, and only he bears the rod of God.
- Aaron: man in his eighties, older brother of Moses; lean, upright build; olive-brown skin; short grey-streaked beard and close-cropped hair; calm, grave face with deep-set eyes. Signature outfit: a long white linen tunic with a blue robe, a woven ephod of blue, purple and scarlet, a breastplate, and a linen headband. Props: none carried alone; the rod of the Exodus is sometimes held.
- the camp of Israel: a wide wilderness encampment of dun-coloured tents of woven goat-hair cloth in ordered rows, with a central sanctuary tent and a gate; bare stony desert plain, scattered acacia and tamarisk, distant dark mountain slopes; a pillar of cloud above the camp by day and fire by night; ash-pits and a clean place beyond its edges.
- Only Moses, Aaron, brother of Moses, the camp of Israel have this canon look; other selected people get clearly different faces, hair and clothing colours.

SCENE PLAN (this moment's place, time and action; obey the rules, brief, canon and style):
Primary subject: Moses and Aaron standing side by side, attentive and still, facing the tabernacle
Action: Moses and Aaron listen as radiance gathers near the tabernacle and spreads gently across the camp.
Setting: Wilderness camp of Israel, tents and the tabernacle among sand and rocky ground with distant desert ridges.
Secondary elements: Israelite families in woven tunics and cloaks standing quietly among the tents; Aaron in linen priestly garments; light and faint cloud drifting from the tabernacle.
Mood: Reverent, attentive and grounded, with quiet awe.
Time of day: Bright midday shifting toward the cooler light of late afternoon, dry clear air and a gentle wind across the camp.
Composition: Wide view from the edge of the camp, with Moses and Aaron in the foreground and the tabernacle and radiance centered in the distance.

ART STYLE: Storybook
Rendering: A modern children's picture-book illustration of the work's world: simplified, softly rounded figures with kind, readable faces, flat shapes with light texture, and clear, uncluttered settings.
Negatives: The illustration fills the whole image: no white border, page edge, vignette or frame, and no title, caption, speech bubble, lettering or signature. Avoid photorealism, anime, 3D rendering and grotesque caricature; faces stay gentle and proportions stay human.
Palette: Warm, soft but saturated colors: honey yellow, terracotta, sage green, dusty blue and cream, with deep indigo for night scenes.
Lighting: Soft, even daylight or a warm glow; simple shadows and no harsh contrast.
Materials and texture: Flat opaque color with light paper grain and pencil texture inside the shapes.
Composition: Simple, readable staging with one clear focus; generous shapes and background that fill the picture to every edge and corner.

- Image 1: Moses's reference sheet (one figure shown in three views). Match its identity exactly for Moses only; do not copy its poses, layout or plain grey background, and give other selected figures a different face and clothing.
- Image 2: the camp of Israel's reference sheet (two views of the same place or thing). Match its identity exactly for the camp of Israel only; do not copy its poses, layout or plain grey background, and give other selected figures a different face and clothing.
- Image 3: Aaron, brother of Moses's reference sheet (one figure shown in three views). Match its identity exactly for Aaron, brother of Moses only; do not copy its poses, layout or plain grey background, and give other selected figures a different face and clothing.
Render everything in the ART STYLE above, even where a reference is painted in another style.

SCENE PRESENTATION:
- Depict the moment directly, as if the viewer is present inside the scene.
- Extend scenery, sky, darkness, architecture or atmosphere all the way to the edges and corners.

SCENE: one moment of The Holy Bible, Matthew 27:35: "When they had crucified him, they divided his clothing among them, casting lots,"

WORK BRIEF (bible-web; what may be shown; it outranks the style, the look and the plan):
Tone: Reverent, grounded and epic; grief, hope and human dignity without spectacle.
Depiction: God the Father has no human face or body; use light, cloud, fire or radiance. The Holy Spirit is dove, wind or flame, never human.
Depiction: Treat battles, death and crucifixion seriously; avoid lingering gore.
Depiction: No sexually explicit content; non-sexual nudity may follow the text.
Depiction: Show all peoples with dignity, without ethnic or religious caricature.
Depiction: Visionary creatures follow the text, strange and fearsome rather than comic.
Era: Roman Judea and the early church
People: Jewish and Gentile Mediterranean communities under Roman rule.
Dress: Tunics, cloaks, priestly robes and Roman military clothing.
Buildings and objects: Stone villages, synagogues, temple, fishing boats and Roman cities.
Technology: Oil lamps, sail and oar, roads, coins and papyrus; no modern objects.

SELECTED CHARACTERS: Jesus Christ, the Son of God and Lord; The Roman soldiers

CANON (fixed identity of the figures, places and things present; the scene plan decides pose, expression and action):
- Jesus: man of about thirty, lean and strong from carpentry and walking; olive-brown skin; dark brown shoulder-length hair parted at centre; short dark beard; calm dark eyes; wears a plain undyed tunic of natural linen with a dark blue-grey cloak and sandals; carries no props except a shepherd's staff when a scene calls for one.
- The Roman soldiers: adult men, late twenties to forties; sturdy, disciplined build; olive to tan skin of Mediterranean men; short-cropped dark or brown hair, clean-shaven or close-cropped beard; stern, weathered faces. Signature dress: a short tunic of undyed linen under a red-brown woollen military cloak, leather belt and sandals, bronze helmet worn at the cohort. Props: a short sword at the hip and a tall rectangular shield.
- Golgotha: a rounded rocky knoll of pale limestone rising just outside the walls of Jerusalem, bare of trees and scrub except for thin dry grass in cracks. Its crown is worn smooth and bony-white, giving the hill its name, the place of a skull. A rough stone-cut quarry face and a few low olive trees stand at its foot, and the walls and towers of the city rise distant behind it.
- Only Jesus Christ, the Son of God and Lord, The Roman soldiers, Golgotha have this canon look; other selected people get clearly different faces, hair and clothing colours.

SCENE PLAN (this moment's place, time and action; obey the rules, brief, canon and style):
Primary subject: Roman soldiers kneeling in the dust beneath the cross, one holding out a cloth while another rolls dice or lots.
Action: Soldiers divide the garments of the crucified man among themselves, casting lots over the pieces.
Setting: Rocky hill of Golgotha outside Jerusalem, with the city walls and roads faintly visible in the distance.
Secondary elements: Three crosses rising behind the soldiers, the central figure's body hung above; scattered tunic cloth and cloaks on the ground, a few spears leaning against stones.
Mood: Grim, weary and indifferent, with a heavy undertone of grief.
Time of day: Midday turning toward afternoon, hot still air with clouds gathering and darkening overhead, harsh light dimming to gloom.
Composition: Wide view from a low angle at ground level, soldiers in the foreground and the cross rising above them against the darkening sky.

ART STYLE: Storybook
Rendering: A modern children's picture-book illustration of the work's world: simplified, softly rounded figures with kind, readable faces, flat shapes with light texture, and clear, uncluttered settings.
Negatives: The illustration fills the whole image: no white border, page edge, vignette or frame, and no title, caption, speech bubble, lettering or signature. Avoid photorealism, anime, 3D rendering and grotesque caricature; faces stay gentle and proportions stay human.
Palette: Warm, soft but saturated colors: honey yellow, terracotta, sage green, dusty blue and cream, with deep indigo for night scenes.
Lighting: Soft, even daylight or a warm glow; simple shadows and no harsh contrast.
Materials and texture: Flat opaque color with light paper grain and pencil texture inside the shapes.
Composition: Simple, readable staging with one clear focus; generous shapes and background that fill the picture to every edge and corner.

REFERENCE IMAGES (attached after this text, in this order; identity and rendering only, never the composition):
- Image 1: Golgotha's reference sheet (two views of the same place or thing). Match its identity exactly for Golgotha only; do not copy its poses, layout or plain grey background, and give other selected figures a different face and clothing.
- Image 2: Jesus Christ, the Son of God and Lord's reference sheet (one figure shown in three views). Match its identity exactly for Jesus Christ, the Son of God and Lord only; do not copy its poses, layout or plain grey background, and give other selected figures a different face and clothing.
Render everything in the ART STYLE above, even where a reference is painted in another style.

NARRATIVE CONTINUITY (cues only; compose the current moment):
- Before: they gave him sour wine to drink mixed with gall. When he had tasted it, he would not drink.
- After: and they sat and watched him there.

SCENE PRESENTATION:
- Depict the moment directly, as if the viewer is present inside the scene.
- Extend scenery, sky, darkness, architecture or atmosphere all the way to the edges and corners.
Aspect ratio: 16:9 (WIDESCREEN landscape).

1) No text or symbols anywhere: no letters, numbers, signage, logos or inscriptions, no writing on scrolls, tablets, books, boards or halos, and no artist's signature or initials in a corner.
2) One scene painted to every edge of the frame: no panels, collage, border, frame, margin, visible paper or blank backdrop, and never a photographed painting or mockup.
3) Nothing from outside the moment's era.
4) Natural anatomy: no extra or malformed limbs, hands or faces.
5) sexually explicit content and lingering gore are never shown; serious depictions of battles, blood, death and crucifixion and non-sexual nudity may be, treated seriously.
6) No likeness of any real actor, performer or public figure.
7) Show the SELECTED CHARACTERS with their canon. Anyone else appears only as an unnamed figure the scene plan describes.
8) A subject without form is never drawn. Only when it is selected may the light, cloud, smoke, fire or wind in the scene plan stand for it, with nobody in them. A throne or seat stays empty unless the scene plan names who sits on it.
If instructions conflict, follow these rules, then the work brief, then canon, then the art style, then the scene plan. The text decides who is in the scene; canon decides how they look; the scene plan decides this moment's place, time, light, clothing and action. Owner look constraints, when given, are binding.

SCENE: one moment of The Holy Bible, described by the scene plan below.

WORK BRIEF (bible-web; what may be shown; it outranks the style, the look and the plan):
Tone: Reverent, grounded and epic; grief, hope and human dignity without spectacle.
Depiction: the presence has no human face or body; use light, cloud, fire or radiance. The Holy Spirit is dove, wind or flame, never human.
Depiction: Treat battles, death and crucifixion seriously; avoid lingering gore.
Depiction: No sexually explicit content; non-sexual nudity may follow the text.
Depiction: Show all peoples with dignity, without ethnic or religious caricature.
Depiction: Visionary creatures follow the text, strange and fearsome rather than comic.
Era: Visionary heaven and renewal
People: Seers, heavenly beings and the redeemed as described.
Dress: Robes and garments with the text's colors and materials.
Buildings and objects: Thrones, altars, glass-like sea and jeweled city as described.
Technology: Ancient lamps, trumpets, harps, swords and sailing ships; no modern objects.

SELECTED CHARACTERS: (none with fixed canon; show only figures the scene plan describes, or none)

UNSEEN PRESENCE (binding): the light, cloud, smoke, fire and wind in the scene plan are light and weather spread through the place, not one glowing shape. Nobody stands, sits or hovers in them.

SCENE PLAN (this moment's place, time and action; obey the rules, brief, canon and style):
Primary subject: A renewed earth of green ground and clear light, with no sea at all in view.
Action: Clear radiance spreads across the new heaven and the new earth, filling the whole sky with steady light that comes from beyond the frame.
Setting: A new heaven above a renewed earth, with no sea, no night and no storm, the land open to a far horizon.
Secondary elements: Glowing cloud and clear light fill the upper sky; the empty place where the sea was is only bright ground; no figures are needed.
Mood: Hopeful, quiet and awe-filled, with a sense of renewal and peace.
Time of day: Radiant, unending day with no night; clear, luminous and windless light holding steady.
Composition: A wide, low panoramic view across the new earth, with the bright heaven filling the upper portion of the frame.

ART STYLE: Storybook
Rendering: A modern children's picture-book illustration of the work's world: simplified, softly rounded figures with kind, readable faces, flat shapes with light texture, and clear, uncluttered settings.
Negatives: The illustration fills the whole image: no white border, page edge, vignette or frame, and no title, caption, speech bubble, lettering or signature. Avoid photorealism, anime, 3D rendering and grotesque caricature; faces stay gentle and proportions stay human.
Palette: Warm, soft but saturated colors: honey yellow, terracotta, sage green, dusty blue and cream, with deep indigo for night scenes.
Lighting: Soft, even daylight or a warm glow; simple shadows and no harsh contrast.
Materials and texture: Flat opaque color with light paper grain and pencil texture inside the shapes.
Composition: Simple, readable staging with one clear focus; generous shapes and background that fill the picture to every edge and corner.

SCENE PRESENTATION:
- Depict the moment directly, as if the viewer is present inside the scene.
- Extend scenery, sky, darkness, architecture or atmosphere all the way to the edges and corners.
Aspect ratio: 16:9 (WIDESCREEN landscape).

effects.planSystem: - Cast marked hasForm: false have no body and are never drawn. When the moment shows one of them appearing or acting, select it and show the moment through the place and the people who witness it. In the scene fields, describe in your own plain words only the physical effects the text names, such as smoke, cloud, fire, storm, wind or light filling a place, spread through the scene or coming from beyond the frame rather than gathered into one glowing shape. Never name it or call it seated, standing, enthroned or riding, and leave out its throne, seat, chariot, robe, train or hem and any face, hands, hair or body: bodily words in the text are metaphors. Say only where those effects are. Whenever the scene keeps light, cloud or fire that comes from it, select it. Keep the people and the place as the subject of the image. A command, oath or mention alone is not an appearance, so add no effect for it then.
effects.planField: For a cast entry with hasForm false, describe only the smoke, cloud, fire, wind or light the text names, never the entry itself.
effects.reviewFault: a hasForm false entry is given a body, face, hands, clothing, a robe or train, a silhouette, a throne or seat of its own, or is described as seated or standing.

checkFigure.direct: true if any face, head, hands, robe, body or human-shaped silhouette appears inside, made of or emerging from light, radiance, cloud, smoke, fire, a pillar or the sky, or seated or standing on a throne, unless it is clearly one of the beings the description names. Look closely at every bright area, cloud and throne; a faint, translucent or partial figure counts. People standing in the scene, and winged angels or creatures the description names, do not count.
checkFigure.describe: true if a head, face, hands, shoulders or a robed or human-shaped body appears inside, made of or emerging from light, radiance, cloud, smoke, fire, a pillar or the sky, or seated or standing on a throne, unless it is clearly one of the beings the description names. A faint or translucent figure counts if you can point to its head, face, hands or body outline. A flame, a heart-shaped glow or billowing cloud is not a figure. People standing in the scene, and winged angels or creatures the description names, do not count.
checkFigure.brightAreas: What is inside each bright area, cloud, fire, pillar or throne, or "none".
